LESSON: AUDIENCE SPEAKING (1 1/

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Audience SPEAKING (1 1/

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Audience SPEAKING (1 1/. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Speak clearly when talking own voice. 2. What should I do to make to others in and out of class. • Learners could be encouraged to myself clear e.g when
2. Demonstrate ability to speak conversations whenever confidently in and out of opportunities arise. class. • In pairs and small groups

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Audience SPEAKING (1 1/ helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Be engaged in c) Demonstrate ability to speak conversations whenever confidently in and out of opportunities arise. class.
2. In pairs and small groups, d) Enjoy speaking to others in learners could be encouraged to and out of class. retell stories told by adults and other learners.
3. Individually and in groups, learners could be involved in presenting songs, poems and rhymes in class and during parade.
4. Be encouraged to make presentations and be appreciated.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
